title: Soft-commit HC ladder & price pivots (May 2026)
content:
Executive summary:

This workbook sketches a lightweight, operational playbook for a "soft-commit" commercial tier (low-duration reserved capacity with flexible swap/burst rights) and the associated headcount ladder required to support it. Goal: quantify how price and commitment-band choices impact runway and staffing needs over a 12‑month rolling window, with particular attention to hysteresis effects when customers downshift from reserved to burst or self-serve.

Key takeaways (short):
- A soft-commit tier priced at "~20% discount vs on-demand with a 3mo rolling notice" materially reduces short-term volatility but increases staffing smoothing requirements (SRE/ops) by ~8–12% versus pure self-serve.
- Token-mix elasticity differs by latency bucket: high-latency (batch embedding) customers are far more price-elastic than low-latency chat workloads; pricing pivots should be bucket-aware.
- Two operational levers reduce HC shock: (1) capacity hedging via temporary contractor pool (6–10% of infra headcount), (2) automated route-based spill policies to cheaper model variants.

Assumptions (model inputs):
- Time horizon: 12 months (Jun 2026–May 2027).
- Baseline ARR mix: 55% self-serve pay-as-you-go, 25% committed reserved, 20% enterprise SLA.
- Average token price (on-demand): $0.0009 / token-equivalent (composite).
- Soft-commit price candidates tested: 10%, 20%, 30% discount to on-demand.
- Typical soft-commit length: 3 months rolling; churn/notice modeled with 45–60 day effective delay.
- Latency buckets: chat (<300ms p50), low-latency (<500ms p95), batch (>500ms). Token mix by bucket: chat 40%, low-latency 35%, batch 25%.
- Capacity multiplier per 1k concurrent chat QPS: 1 unit; for batch, 0.25 units.

Model structure (light):
- Forecast token demand by segment -> convert to required GPU units using bucket multipliers -> map to committed vs burst capacity by scenario -> compute staffing overlay for on-call, runbook, infra ops scaling (SRE + infra engineers), add 15% overhead for platform and applied ML.
- Hysteresis: when customers downshift from reserved to self-serve we apply a 2–4 week spike in bursts (cache misses, re-priming KV caches), modeled as 1.4x short-term token demand for affected customers over 14 days.

Scenario snapshots (selected rows from the sheet):

Scenario A (20% soft-commit discount - conservative uptake)
- Soft-commit uptake: 18% of baseline tokens shift into soft-commit band over 3 months.
- Effective monthly revenue change: +5% vs baseline (mix shift to committed pricing but lower per-token).
- Required infra HC (mid-year): +9% SRE/ops headcount vs baseline to maintain SLAs due to hedging and smoothing.
- Runway impact (12m): +0.6 months (improves marginally due to committed revenue).

Scenario B (10% discount - low adoption)
- Uptake: 9% of tokens.
- Revenue impact: +1.8% vs baseline.
- Infra HC change: +4% (smaller smoothing).
- Runway impact: +0.15 months.

Scenario C (30% discount - aggressive pricing to win share)
- Uptake: 34% of tokens (significant migration from enterprise and self-serve).
- Revenue impact: -6% vs baseline in first 6 months (loss on per-token margin), picks up to -1% at 12 months assuming retention and upsell.
- Infra HC change: +17% (larger absolute capacity and monitoring burden).
- Runway impact: -1.2 months (worsens short-term burn).

Headcount ladder (phasing sketch):
- Baseline (Jun 2026): infra ops 18, SRE 12, applied ML infra 6, platform eng 10, support/CS coverage 14 (total infra-adj: 60).
- Soft-commit +20% uptake (12 months): infra ops -> +2 contractors (convertible), SRE +1 FTE, platform eng +1, support +2 (customer onboarding for soft-commit).
- Soft-commit +30% uptake: infra ops +4 contractors +2 FTE, SRE +3 FTE, platform eng +3 FTE, support +5 FTE.

Cost sensitivity table (excerpt):
- Variable cost per token (GPU + infra) baseline: $0.00045.
- Soft-commit margin at 10% discount: 49% contribution.
- Soft-commit margin at 20% discount: 36% contribution.
- Soft-commit margin at 30% discount: 24% contribution.
- Break-even token price (with fixed HC and op costs) requires adoption >28% at 20% discount.

Latency-bucket elasticity (observed / simulated):
- Batch: price elasticity -1.6 (demand drops 16% per 10% price increase).
- Chat: price elasticity -0.4.
- Low-latency: -0.9.
Implication: discounts targeted at batch-heavy customers yield bigger volume but lower immediate CPU intensity relative to chat.

Operational mitigations (implementation playbook):
- Instrumentation: add a "soft-commit tag" in billing events and tracing so we can measure hysteresis spike windows and cache cold-starts. (Linked ticket: JIRA-FIN-1248 / infra-telemetry epic).
- Capacity hedge: maintain a rolling contractor pool equal to 8% of infra ops capacity during first 6 months of launch; convert to FTE if adoption >22% sustained for 2 months.
- Auto-route policy: for soft-commit requests during surge, prefer quantized model variant where quality loss <2% on eval set; target 12–18% cost reduction when spilled.
- Pricing guardrail: cap soft-commit discount at 20% unless accompanied by minimum term or volume minimums; allow negotiated enterprise exceptions.

Customer-facing mechanics (draft):
- Offer a 3mo rolling soft-commit with 45-day cancellation notice. Customers get a usage credit bucket; unused credits convert to scaled pay-as-you-go at month-end at full price.
- Provide analytics portal: expected savings, burst-use history, and recommended minimums based on their token mix.

Open questions / risks:
- Will enterprise customers re-contract to soft-commit and create downstream SLA complexity? (sales ops risk).
- Does contractor hedge meaningfully reduce SLA incidents or just shift toil? Need a 60-day pilot.
- Is weaning off deep-discounted soft-commit customers operationally feasible without long-term margin erosion?

Next steps (owner + timing):
- [Aisha] Deliver full model workbook with per-customer simulation (two sample enterprise customers) by 2026-05-24.
- [Marcus] Instrument billing events with soft-commit tag (infra telemetry) - PR targeted 2026-06-07.
- [Sofia] Draft customer T&C and marketing copy for soft-commit offer by 2026-06-10.
- Run 60-day pilot with 3 existing enterprise customers that have mixed batch/chat mix; monitor hysteresis metrics and CS onboarding effort.

Appendix (quick notes):
- Quick sensitivity: if token unit cost falls 12% (hardware improvements / quant pipelines), soft-commit margin at 20% discount flips positive across adoption curves tested.
- Reference analysis: capacity-simulator run id 2026-05-softcommit-v3 (github: infra/capacity-simulator#1023).

Unresolved inputs to finalize model:
- precise FS EV/contract conversion logic (how unused credits are reconciled on books),
- latency-to-GPU-unit mapping for new quantized variants,
- sales uplift multiplier for offering (engineering estimate required).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally compact — the workbook linked in the artifacts contains the full per-customer sheets and the Monte Carlo sweep used to produce the percentile HC deltas. Requesting feedback on the pricing guardrail (20% cap) and the contractor hedge sizing.
